questions_and_answers.question_text: What does the ending -xialai add to zhù?
How do bāng máng and bāngzhu differ in register?
What kind of phrase is bāng máng?
How is the person helped expressed with bāng máng?
Write the Chinese for "Help me a little."
Give the three ways to say "He helps me."

answers.answer_text: Tā bāngzhu wǒ; Tā bāng wǒde máng; Tā gěi wǒ bāng máng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Why don't you just stay at my house?"

answers.answer_text: Nǐ jiù zài wǒ jiā zhùxialai ba!

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of bāng máng?
Write the Chinese for "Nobody wants to go with me. All I can do is go by myself."

answers.answer_text: Dàjiā dōu bù yuànyi péi wǒ qù, wǒ zhǐ hǎo yíge rén qù le.

articles.text:
9. A: Nǐ zhùxialai ba, yě kěyi gěi  Stay (live) here and you can help us
      wǒmen bāng diǎnr máng.        a bit.
   B: Wǒ báitian yǒu kè, zhǐ hǎo   I have classes during the day; I can
      wǎnshang zuò diǎnr shì.       only work at night.

Notes on No. 9

zhùxialai: "to stay; to settle down" in a place. Zhù can either mean "to live, to reside" or just "to stay" TEMPORARILY. The ending -xialai adds the meaning of COMING TO REST, not going away.

Méi guānxi, nǐ jiù zài wǒ jiā    That's all right, why don't you just
zhùxialai ba!                    stay at my house?

bāng máng: "to help; help." Both bāng máng and bāngzhu are very common. BĀNGZHU is a little more FORMAL than BĀNG MÁNG, which is purely CONVERSATIONAL.

Bāng máng is a VERB-OBJECT phrase (literally, "help-busy" — "help me in my busy-ness"):

Bāng wǒ yìdiǎnr máng.            Help me a little.
Wǒ zài Měiguode shíhou, tā       He helped me a lot when I was in
bāngle wǒ bù shǎo máng.          America.

Bāngzhu, however, is JUST A VERB. The word order is therefore SIMPLER:

Tā bāngzhu wǒ.                   "He helps me."
BUT Tā bāng wǒde máng.
OR  Tā gěi wǒ bāng máng.

When bāng máng is used, the person helped is expressed either (1) in a phrase MODIFYING máng or (2) in a PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE with gěi.

zhǐ hǎo: "can only, have no choice but to"

Xià zhème dàde yǔ, wǒmen zhǐ     Since it's raining so hard, we have no
hǎo bú qù le.                    choice but not to go.
Dàjiā dōu bù yuànyi péi wǒ qù,   Nobody wants to go with me. All I can
wǒ zhǐ hǎo yíge rén qù le.       do is go by myself.
